key_insight: The contact-energy cost Hamiltonian used in quantum protein structure prediction is not reliably aligned with structural accuracy, so a good quantum optimizer may still optimize the wrong objective.
engineering_relevance: For quantum algorithm design, this shows that validating the cost Hamiltonian itself is as important as improving the quantum solver, especially for application-driven optimization problems.
method: Compared a lattice-based protein contact-energy Hamiltonian with structural error measured by RMSD to experimentally determined structures.
Analyzed small peptides directly and used Monte Carlo sampling to estimate correlations for larger instances.
Examined how adding more interaction shells affects alignment between energy and structural accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports weak average correlation for small peptides, with correlation improving for larger instances and when more interaction shells are included.
watch_item: The results suggest the cost Hamiltonian may be a poor proxy for true structure quality in small cases, so hardware performance alone should not be used to claim predictive success.
paper_title: Assessing Cost Hamiltonian Reliability in Quantum Protein Structure Prediction
